questions.question: 1. What is the space complexity of the merge sort algorithm?

explanations.a: Correct. Merge sort needs extra space to temporarily store merged results. The total extra space needed is proportional to the size of the array, so the space complexity is O(N).
explanations.b: Incorrect. The extra space needed is much less than 2^N.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Merge sort is not an in-place algorithm. It needs extra space to merge arrays.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The extra space needed is much less than N^2, because the same temporary space is reused for subarrays.

questions.question: 2. Consider the array: A = [8, 7, -2, 4, 1, 100, 0, -1]. Which of the following pairs of subarrays are merged together at some point during merge sort (assume ascending order)?

explanations.a: Incorrect. These subarrays are separated early and only come together in the final merge, not as a pair.
explanations.b: Correct. [7, 8] and [-2, 4] are merged together during the merge sort process.
explanations.c: Incorrect. These subarrays are not merged directly as a pair.
explanations.d: Incorrect. These subarrays are separated early and only come together in the final merge.

questions.question: 3. Why is the time complexity of merge sort O(N log N)?

answers.a: N for dividing the array and log(N) for the number of division steps.
answers.b: N for merging subarrays and log(N) for the number of merge steps.
answers.c: N for the number of division steps and log(N) for dividing the array.
answers.d: N for the number of merge steps and log(N) for merging subarrays.

explanations.a: Incorrect. Dividing the array is fast and does not take much time.
explanations.b: Correct. Each merge step processes all N elements, and there are about log(N) merge steps.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The number of division steps is not N, and dividing is fast.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Merging takes more time than log(N), and there are fewer than N merge steps.
